newsitem.title: ISRAEL: ISRAELI SHARES CLOSE LOWER ON CPI AND WALL STREET.
newsitem.headline: ISRAELI SHARES CLOSE LOWER ON CPI AND WALL STREET.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower on Wednesday on fears of a high July consumer price index (CPI) and on Wall Street's large declines on Tuesday, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares lost 1.70 percent, or 5.15 points, to 297.67 on an all-share turnover of 156 million shekels against 143 million shekels on Monday, the last day of trading before the Jewish fast day of Tisha B'Av.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.36 percent lower at 304.55.
"The market has its eyes on July's CPI, which will be published on Friday, and on what Wall Street will do," said Tiki Haddad of IBI Investment House.
"Traders fear that if there is a crash on Wall Street it will spill over to markets all over the world," she said.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 101.27 points on Tuesday.
July's CPI is expected to post a large increase of 1.0 to 1.2 percent, traders said.
"If the CPI will be lower than 0.9 percent then we don't expect a change in interest rates at the end of the month and the market will react positively," said a trader at Solid Financial Markets.
"But if the CPI is around one percent or higher, then we expect a rate hike of 0.3 to 0.5 percentage point," the trader said.
The base rate stands now at 12.7 percent on an annual basis.
Teva Pharmaceutical Industries fell 4.25 percent to 19,947 agorot (Israeli cents) following its slide on Wall Street on Monday and Tuesday, Haddad said.
On Tuesday Teva said it had suspended sales of antibiotic Clindamycin because of a warning letter from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration about manufacturing issues.

Koor Industries fell 1.0 percent to 37,006 agorot. Haddad said the share would have fallen even more on the company's decline on Wall Street. But rumours that Koor's main shareholder Bank Hapoalim was interested in spinning off some of its subsidiaries prevented a further decline.
Haddad said the banking sector attracted a lot of attention on estimates that the shares were undervalued.
The most active shares were Koor, with volume of 12 million shekels; Bank Leumi, which lost 0.75 percent to 579 agorot on turnover of 8.8 million shekels; and Teva with volume of 8.2 million shekels.
- Shoshanna Solomon, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233 SAS TCC
